headline: Dhaka attacks: Crude bomb blasts and arson attacks aimed at spreading panic, says DMP
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police are investigating a series of explosions and vehicle fires across the capital, targeting police stations and headquarters.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that recent crude bomb explosions and arson attacks on public transport across the capital are designed to create public panic.
Targets included the CID headquarters and the Pallabi police station, where crude bombs were thrown and exploded on the premises.
Police have arrested several individuals, including members of banned organizations and their affiliated bodies, in connection with these incidents.
DMP Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Aktar Hossain confirmed that a particular group is deliberately carrying out these acts of sabotage to spread fear.
In response, the DMP has increased police deployment, strengthened operational activities, and deployed mobile patrol teams and police pickets.
The Detective Branch (DB) has already arrested several people with bomb-making materials and explosives.
Authorities are currently analyzing CCTV footage to identify suspects and are monitoring the purchase of flammable substances from petrol pumps.
Law enforcement activities and drives continue as the police work to ensure public safety and dispel fear among residents.
caption:
Crude bombs and bus fires across Dhaka are deliberate attempts to spread panic, according to the DMP.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that recent crude bomb explosions and arson attacks on public transport across the capital are designed to create public panic.

Targets included the CID headquarters and the Pallabi police station, where crude bombs were thrown and exploded on the premises.

Police have arrested several individuals, including members of banned organizations and their affiliated bodies, in connection with these incidents.

DMP Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Aktar Hossain confirmed that a particular group is deliberately carrying out these acts of sabotage to spread fear.

In response, the DMP has increased police deployment, strengthened operational activities, and deployed mobile patrol teams and police pickets.

The Detective Branch (DB) has already arrested several people with bomb-making materials and explosives.

Authorities are currently analyzing CCTV footage to identify suspects and are monitoring the purchase of flammable substances from petrol pumps.

Law enforcement activities and drives continue as the police work to ensure public safety and dispel fear among residents.

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: BOESL: [[Malaysia-bound workers will pay nothing]] for migration
headline: BOESL: Malaysia-bound workers will pay nothing for migration
summary: A digital lottery has shortlisted 300 candidates for 112 jobs at DHL Supply Chain Malaysia under a zero-cost recruitment initiative.
details: The state-run Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) has introduced a zero-cost recruitment initiative for workers heading to Malaysia. Under this program, Malaysian companies will bear all migration expenses, including medical fees and airfares.

To ensure transparency, BOESL used a digital lottery system to shortlist 300 candidates from 4,039 applicants for 112 jobs at DHL Supply Chain Malaysia. The roles include operations assistants and technical staff with a monthly basic salary of 1,700 ringgit.

From the 300 shortlisted candidates, the employer will finally select 112 workers based on skills, qualifications, and performance in practical examinations and face-to-face interviews scheduled for November 12 to 15.
Selected workers will undergo three days of company-provided training before their departure, with the first flight expected in the first week of December.
BOESL Managing Director Mohammad Rashedul Hasan emphasized that 'Zero means zero,' warning applicants against making payments to anyone, as no financial transactions are required for recruitment.

This effort is part of a broader government initiative to send 10,000 workers to Malaysia at zero migration cost. BOESL has already received demand orders for 558 workers across sectors like manufacturing, tourism, and technical assistance.
Regarding previous recruitment processes, BOESL confirmed that workers who failed to travel before the May 31, 2024 deadline will not receive priority under this new initiative.
